candidates.label: Global monotonic commit cursor and graph-wide consistent cut
evidence: Per-subject streams require one deterministic high-water mark so replay computes the same graph rather than a timing-dependent mix of subject states.

candidates.label: Causally closed graph cut from exact event dependency references
evidence: Explicit causal dependencies can assemble a coherent graph without one global event order, at the cost of dependency-closure and conflict machinery.

candidates.label: Join whatever subject snapshot is latest when queried
evidence: Independent latest snapshots can advance at different times and expose relation endpoints or invariants from incompatible graph versions.
rejectionReasons: A timing-dependent join is not deterministic and can calculate a fractured ontology that never existed at one coherent event boundary.

candidates.label: Defer graph-assembly consistency
evidence: Deferral preserves the per-subject stream decision but blocks a deterministic ontology projection.

candidates.label: Stop the per-subject stream design
evidence: Stopping terminates this stream topology without implementation effects.
